entry.title: Java Concurrency LLD: Build a Custom BlockingQueue From Scratch
entry.summary:
Java Concurrency LLD: Build a Custom BlockingQueue From Scratch
At Apple and Amazon, implementing a thread-safe BlockingQueue is one of the most frequent concurrency challenges in Low-Level Design (LLD) interviews. It immediately exposes whether you understand thread coordination, thread-safe state mutation, and JVM internals, or merely rely on off-the-shelf utilities. Relying on intrinsic locks (synchronized) with notifyAll(), which triggers the "thundering herd" problem by waking up both producers and consumers simultaneously. Checking capacity bounds using an if statement instead of a while loop, leaving the queue vulnerable to state corruption via spurious wakeups. Failing to structure lock acquisition with a proper try-finally block, which causes unrecoverable deadlocks if a thread …

entry.title: NocoBase updates by primary key, not by your filter
entry.summary: If you have used Django, you know there are two ways to update many rows, and you pick one on purpose. QuerySet.update() sends one SQL statement. It does not call save(), and it does not emit pre_save or post_save. Looping over objects and calling Model.save() does the opposite: one statement per row, signals fire, and it is slower. Neither is always right. You choose based on whether anything is listening. NocoBase does not offer that choice. Every filtered bulk update goes through the second shape — and it costs more than speed. Test setup: NocoBase 2.2.7 (official Docker image) + PostgreSQL 16. SQL was captured with log_statement=all. Vibe coding has always been a weird topic to talk about. Lately it's gotten even weirder.
